page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Below it, two medallion portraits side by side, each with its legend (illustrations with printed legends). Below them, one column of running text with two paragraphs, then the signature at the lower right.

main_text.p: CHILDERICVS, huius nominis tertius, dictus stupidus,ob ignauiā, fratri suo Theodorico secūdo supradicto,succedit in regno Franciae anno mundi 4703. à Christo nato 741. hoc principe,Gripho hæreditate Martelli patris priuatus,Laudunum arce belli occupauerat,mox fratribus in fide se permittere cogitur. Carolomanus eius frater Roma rediens, abiectis omnibus fortunis,in cœnobium secessit:deinde in monte Cassinum migrauit,tonsu,habituq; monachi.Childericus anno regni nono,cum regio nomine indignus ac solij dehonestamentum videretur,opera Pipini consilióque Zachariæ, Pontificis, regno pellitur:conuentu præterea habito,mira procerum consensione Pipinus ipse salutatur Rex:Childericus fit monachus. Vide Æmy.lib.2.Chroni.Reg.Franc.Gag.lib.3.defecit primum in hoc Childerico masculea Regum Francorum progenies.

PIPINVS Breuis, Francorum Rex dicitur anno mundi 4712. à Christo nato 750. Pipini præsidium contra Aistulfum Longobardorum Regem Papa implorat:coscripto exercitu Pipinus Italiā intrat: Aistulfum Papiæ obsidet, atque ad deditionem cogit. Papæ exarchatum Rauennatem dono dat, monitis etiā Constantini Copronymi Imperatoris neglectis. Vide Blon. lib.1.Dec.2.Æmy.li.2. Aistulfus Longobardorum Rex inter venandum obiit. Rex Pipinus Parlamentū in Frācia instituit:Pariliis[?] obiit anno regni 18. relictis filiis Regibus, Carolo Magno & Carolomano:succedit ei in Franciae regno Carolus Magnus anno mundi 4730. à Christo nato 768. qui imperat Romae anno mundi 4763. de quo,vt Imperatore,suo loco meminerimus: à Pharamundo ad Pipinum sunt anni 331. à Meroueo 302. à Clodoueo Christiano 252.

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits (Childericus, left; Pipinus, right) and are not transcribed beyond their printed legends. "Pariliis" is doubtful (probably Parisiis). The first word of the second paragraph is printed in capitals. Printed hyphens and abbreviations are kept as printed.
